summary: INT8 per-row scale quantization is viable. 4× compression achieved. Matvec parity acceptable (cosine ≥ 0.999 on all tested layers). Single-layer microbench shows INT8 matvec ≈ FP32 speed (~1.01×). No runtime integration yet. Phase 14B: integrate INT8 sidecar loading into llama.cpp PRT path.

int8_per_row_scale.avx2_vnni: Dequant to float + float AVX2 (or VNNI direct)

first_prototype.per_row_definition: one float32 scale per hidden dimension (K scales total, K=hidden)
first_prototype.file_format: [M*K bytes int8 data] + [K*4 bytes float32 scales]

quantization_tool.inputs: float32 sidecar dir, output dir, model, layers
quantization_tool.outputs: int8 sidecar files + metadata JSON + error metrics
quantization_tool.fixed_bugs: Axis bug found and fixed — initial quantization used wrong axis for per-row scales (per column instead of per row)

key_finding: INT8 matvec is essentially same speed as FP32 matvec (ratio ~1.005× for 3B, ~0.991× for 0.5B) while using 4× less memory. This is because both are memory-bandwidth bound. The dequantization overhead is negligible compared to memory access time. At multi-layer scale, 4× less memory traffic should translate to proportionally less wall time.
what_this_phase_proves: Packed sidecar format is defined: INT8 per-row scale with K float32 scales
Quantization conversion works on both 0.5B and 3B layers
4× compression achieved with negligible quality loss (cosine ≥ 0.999)
INT8 matvec parity acceptable (output cosine ≥ 0.999 on all tested layers)
INT8 matvec single-layer speed is essentially identical to FP32 (~1× ratio)
Dequantization overhead is negligible (both paths are memory-bandwidth bound)
what_this_phase_does_not_prove: No guarantee that single-layer speed parity translates to multi-layer inference speedup

phase13_comparison.int8_expectation: ~4× less memory traffic; kernel time similar; if memory-bound, wall should improve
phase13_comparison.note: Cannot claim speedup yet — need runtime canary with INT8 sidecars in llama.cpp

allowed_claims: INT8 sidecar quantization achieves 4× compression with output cosine ≥ 0.999 on tested layers
INT8 matvec is single-layer timing-equivalent to float32 matvec (~1× ratio)
INT8 quantization pipeline is validated for 0.5B and 3B sidecar layers
forbidden_claims: No end-to-end speedup claim from INT8 sidecars
recommended_next: Phase 14B: INT8 Packed Sidecar Runtime Canary — integrate INT8 sidecar loading into llama.cpp PRT path, implement dequantization in custom op, run single-layer runtime canary, then full 3B generation test with INT8 sidecars.
